correctness.rationale: For centrally symmetric convex K, the radial function is positive Lipschitz; the boundary angular density q/P is valid a.e. The origin-near segments must be near antipodal. The distance is uniformly r(theta)|delta|/2+O(delta²); Lebesgue differentiation and dominated convergence yield the 4/P² integral. A pointwise algebraic identity yields exact deficit and 1/2 bound for q/(q+r). Lipschitz zero derivative implies disk. The smooth strictly convex radial perturbation proves factor-2 optimal. Square quadrant integral and numerical checker independently agree. An independent square check using the opposite-side endpoint diamond, rather than the polar density, reproduces the coefficient exactly.

originality.rationale: Actual published-finding corpus searches and accessible own ledger compared to distinct objects and implications. Primary Bäsel full PDF uses invariant random lines, not independent perimeter endpoints. Full published triangle and rectangle interception texts use homothetic polygon targets, not centered Euclidean disk, and do not imply the universal arbitrary-body radial energy or its sharp stability constant. Historical priority remains provisional. The potentially relevant Ehlers and Enns (1981) article was accessible only by abstract after bounded lawful retrieval attempts; its general length formulas could encode additional information, so priority remains expressly provisional.
residual_risks: Historical literature on noncircular endpoint-uniform boundary chords may be indexed under alternative geometric-tomography terminology; full priority cannot be certified by finite search.

The 2014 random-chord-and-containment paper of D. Ren was located by abstract but its full text was not available in the present source inspections; its stated models differ, but this remains an access risk.
Finite numerical tests verify shape examples, not the universal theorem; no independent human verification has occurred.

Ehlers and Enns (1981) is the closest older surface-random chord source; its complete ten-page text was inaccessible after arXiv/open-access searches and an authorized institutional-access attempt. Only its abstract was inspected; any implicit implication from its general formulas remains a real historical priority risk.

value.rationale: Independent perimeter-boundary chord sampling is a standard and demonstrably different chord convention. The local likelihood of penetrating a central sensor is a natural stochastic-geometric observable. The theorem gives an exact general all-convex-body intensity, a unique disk minimizer at fixed perimeter, and a sharp nonlinear radial-energy quantitative stability, so the statement is a structural extremal theorem rather than a routine circle or square exercise.
